rationale: Good product spec, not yet implementable. Three of four P0 items rest on a false statement about existing behaviour (jobs are already durable; verify already reconciles live vs disk; the account record has no priority field), two acceptance criteria are unsatisfiable or misworded, and the two cited evidence sources (the 142-mp4 tour screenshot and the real export tree) disagree. The items are individually small and worth keeping; the premises and acceptance must be rewritten before coding.

top3.action: Rewrite the P0-1/P0-2 premises from source and narrow the scope. Jobs already persist (server/store.js:170-173, 509-511) and verify.py already computes per-area live/exported/missing (python/worker/verify.py:264-276). P0-2 becomes 'render account.verify.areas with an explicit unread state and add bytes/last-export', not a new manifest-backed matrix; P0-1 becomes 'surface the existing job records plus a retry that requeues the statuses markStaleJobs creates (store.js:206)', because today a restart strands running jobs as unknown and the pool never requeues them.

Make the acceptance criteria executable. P0-1 names a 'failed' job state that does not exist (statuses are queued/running/twofa/done/error/invalid/unknown/cancelled). P0-2 says the matrix equals 'manifest.sqlite3 summary and file counts' for example.harvest, but those differ by construction: manifest status='done' is 104 photos / 9 hidden, disk is 124 / 18, because 29 live-photo .mp4 proxies have no manifest row. State one definition of downloaded (assets vs files) and assert the same number in both places.
top3.verified_by: manifest query + ls on export/example.harvest@icloud.com; server/socket/worker-pool.js:1108

top3.action: Build the two persistence primitives before their UI. For P0-3 add priority/order/note to defaultAccount and to updateAccount's allowlist and insert by order (today updateAccount drops all three silently and enqueue() unshifts). For P0-4 add reason and attempt columns to the manifest with an explicit ALTER TABLE (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS will not migrate an existing DB), and never overwrite a good file's row with failed/size 0.

what_would_change: A real verify run on example.harvest that populates verify.areas would weaken the 'counts is the only number you have' half of COR-3, though not the export_done overwrite itself.
Evidence that the tour screenshots came from a tree matching the 142-mp4 claim (no such files exist under export/) would revive P1-1's premise and raise the score by roughly one point.
A production socket restart showing the startup wave re-exporting the stranded account would lower COR-4's blast radius to a lost auth flow rather than a stuck account.
A stated deployment Node version >= 22.5 with a busy_timeout set on the manifest reader would remove the main open question on P0-2's implementation cost.
